newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian military pilots to get laser training.
newsitem.headline: Canadian military pilots to get laser training.

text.p: The Canadian military will soon give its pilots training and visors to protect them from eye-damaging lasers, a defence official said on Friday.

The danger lasers pose to air force personnel was highlighted by an April 4 incident in which a Russian cargo ship was suspected of aiming a laser at a Canadian military helicopter, temporarily damaging the eyes of the Canadian pilot and his American passenger.
Jeff Helps, general safety officer at Air Command headquarters in Winnipeg, said the new training had been planned before the incident.
"But this was the impetus to make it happen a little faster," he added.
A select group of Canadian military pilots previously received an intensive six-day training course on the use of lasers.
Patricia Low-Bedard, a spokeswoman at the Department of Foreign Affairs, said on Friday that Canada did not intend to protest to Russia over the April 4 incident.
"We have concluded the evidence is inconclusive," said Low-Bedard. "So we have decided not to raise the issue formally with Russia."
